questions.q: Which six fields make up every journal header in General Ledger?
options: Account, debit, credit, description, status, approver
Ledger, journal name, accounting date, source, category, currency
Legal entity, business unit, data access set, currency, period, status
Batch, line, account, amount, source, approver
questions.explain: Every journal header carries ledger, journal name, accounting date, source, category, and currency.

questions.q: What does the Source field default to when you're entering a journal by hand?
options: Manual
Spreadsheet
Payables
Allocation
questions.explain: Source defaults to Manual for a hand-entered journal.

questions.q: What must be true for General Ledger to let you mark a journal complete?
options: Only the grand total of debits and credits must match
The journal must already be posted
The journal must use the Manual source only
Debits must equal credits for every balancing segment value represented, not just the grand total
questions.explain: General Ledger checks that debits equal credits within each balancing segment value, not merely in aggregate.

questions.q: What is the difference between Save and Complete/Submit for a journal?
options: Save posts the journal; Complete deletes it
They are identical actions with different labels
Save stores a draft you can keep editing; Complete marks it ready to post or route for approval
Save requires approval; Complete does not
questions.explain: Save keeps a journal as an editable draft. Complete/Submit moves it toward posting or approval.

questions.q: Can a single journal line carry both a debit and a credit amount?
options: No, a line carries either a debit or a credit amount, never both
Yes, always
Only on the first line of a batch
Only for intercompany lines
questions.explain: Each journal line is one account combination with either a debit or a credit amount — never both on the same line.
